definitions.explanation: Supernatural powers or practices involving spells and incantations. Also used for stage magic and illusions, though 手品 is more common for that meaning.

examples.japanese: その{少年|しょうねん}は{魔術|まじゅつ}{学校|がっこう}に{通|かよ}っている。
examples.english: The boy attends a school of sorcery.

examples.japanese: {中世|ちゅうせい}ヨーロッパでは、{魔術|まじゅつ}を{使|つか}ったとされる{人々|ひとびと}が{厳|きび}しく{罰|ばっ}せられた。
examples.english: In medieval Europe, people accused of practicing sorcery were severely punished.

notes:
USAGE:
Frequently encountered in fantasy fiction, anime, and games. Also used historically for actual occult practices. In modern usage, {魔術|まじゅつ} has a darker, more supernatural connotation compared to {魔法|まほう}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {魔術|まじゅつ}を{使|つか}う (to use magic)
- {魔術|まじゅつ}{師|し} (sorcerer, magician)
- {魔術|まじゅつ}を{学|まな}ぶ (to learn sorcery)
- {黒|くろ}{魔術|まじゅつ} (black magic)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {魔法|まほう}: magic — more general and often lighter in tone; common in fairy tales
- {手品|てじな}: magic tricks — stage magic, sleight of hand
- {呪術|じゅじゅつ}: sorcery, curse magic — emphasizes curses and shamanistic practices
